item.title: Councillor says South Kerry greenway will be "most spectacular" in Ireland ahead of historic opening
item.description: The South Kerry greenway will be the most spectacular in Ireland. That's according to the cathaoirleach of the Kenmare Municipal District (MD), Norma Moriarty. The first section of the greenway, between Golden’s of Kells and the old Kells Railway Station will open to the public tomorrow and will be fully accessible to both pedestrians and cyclists. item.title: Kerry County Council invites expressions of interest for development of affordable housing
item.description: Kerry County Council has officially published an invitation to developers and builders to express interest in building affordable housing in this county. Kerry councillors have been critical of the slow rollout of the government’s affordable housing scheme in this county. This initial call for expressions of interest will be limited to the urban areas of Tralee and Killarney. item.title: Road safety campaigners express frustration over government u-turn on RSA overhaul
item.description: Road safety groups are upset and frustrated by the government’s u-turn on its decision to disband the RSA. That’s according to Dr Vinne Wall of the Cork Cycling Campaign. He was reacting after Junior Transport Minister Sean Canney said plans to split the Road Safety Authority in two have been reversed. Advertisement Dr Wall believes there needs to be a separate group established to provide specific expertise to improve road safety. He says an overhaul is needed as the RSA is not fit for purpose.

item.title: 35-year old Cork man sentenced after punching Kerry publican in the back of head
item.description: A 35-year old Cork man has been sentenced to nine months in prison after punching a Kerry publican in the back of the head. Noel Bowen of 12 Park View, Carrignavar, in County Cork was accused of punching Ray Madden at O’Connell’s Cove Bar in Caherdaniel on 24th August last year (2024). Outlining the facts of the case, Inspector Fergal Long told Judge David Waters at Tralee District Court that the defendant was behaving loudly in the bar and annoying staff. item.title: Xeinadin acquires Killarney-based cloud-accounting practice
item.description: Xeinadin, a professional services firm in Ireland and the UK, has acquired a Kerry-based cloud-accounting practice. Killarney-based O’Rourke & Co is joining Xeinadin’s team. Founded in 2011, O’Rourke & Co specialises in cloud and digital accounting to support small and medium-sized businesses. item.title: Man fined for offences including public disorder during Kerry senior football team homecoming
item.description: A 34-year-old Tralee man has been fined €1,100.00 for the possession of drugs and public order offences. item.title: OPW rejects proposal for earlier opening of Skellig Michael to visitors
item.description: The Office of Public Works has said it cannot extend the visitor season for Skellig Michael earlier than the traditional mid-May opening. It followed a call by Fianna Fáil councillor Norma Moriarty at November’s Kerry County Council meeting. A response to the council from the OPW was shared with county councillors at December’s monthly meeting. item.title: Over 141,000 passengers travelled through Kerry Airport in the third quarter of 2025
item.description: Over 141,000 passengers travelled through Kerry Airport in the third quarter of this year. That’s according to figures released from the Central Statistics Office. The report shows more than 224,000 passengers have gone through the doors of Kerry Airport in the first nine months of the year.
